WORKING NOTES — Inventory ordering

Demand: Observed sales: 6,4,8,0,11,1,0,3,2. Stockouts lost 22 units on days 4,6,7,8,10, so true demand is higher. Estimate ~6/day, variable with spikes to 11. Plan for 6–8/day.

Costs:
- Holding ~0.067/unit/day.
- Ordering fixed 0.50/order.
- Stockout 1.00/lost unit. Stockout cost is much higher than holding, so prioritize availability.

Lead time/arrivals:
- Orders take ~2 days. “Arriving over next 2 days” means [today, tomorrow].
- Stockouts occurred when stock hit 0 before receipts. A Day 7 order of 8 still had stockout because it arrived too late.

Policy lessons:
- Maintain inventory position (on hand + on order) at least 2 days of expected demand plus safety buffer. Target ~15–20 units.
- Reorder when position falls below ~15. Order enough to restore target. Fixed ordering cost is small, so do not delay if stockout risk exists.
- Do not order 0 when stock is low. If projected stock before next receipt cannot cover today/tomorrow demand, order now.
- Cycle counts matched system; no adjustment needed. Ops notes are mostly irrelevant to ordering.

Current: Day 10 stock 6, arrivals [1,4]. Demand likely ~6–8/day. Risk remains; order to restore buffer.

WORKING NOTES — Inventory ordering

Demand: Recent 14 days: 1,0,3,2,7,4,0,2,4,3,9,4,7,6. Variable, with spikes 9–11. Lost sales understate true demand. Plan for 7–9/day, be ready for 10+.

Costs: Holding 0.067/unit/day. Ordering 0.50/order. Stockout 1.00/lost unit. Stockouts dominate costs, so prioritize availability over holding/order savings.

Lead time/arrivals: Orders take ~2 days. Arrivals may come after daily sales, so same-day receipts do not prevent stockout. “Arriving over next 2 days” is not reliable protection if on hand is low.

Policy lessons:
- Track inventory position = on hand + on order, but stockouts still happened when position looked adequate because arrivals were too late or demand spiked.
- Target position ~20–25 units: cover 7–9/day for 2 days plus safety for spikes.
- Reorder when position falls below ~18–20. If stock is 0–5, order at least 14–20 immediately; do not wait.
- Small orders of 7–9 when stock is low caused repeated stockouts (Days 17, 18, 20 lost 8–9 units).
- Day 12 order of 14 still had stockout 4; aim higher when stock is already 0.
- Ops notes (temp receiving, racking, carrier pickup, cycle count) are irrelevant; counts matched system.

Current: Stock often hits 0 before receipts. Maintain high buffer. When stock is 3 and arrivals are [4,7], order now to restore position to 20+.

WORKING NOTES — Inventory ordering

Demand rose: last 14 days 9,4,7,6,7,7,12,18,2,15,11,0,18,3; avg ~8.5, spikes 12–18. Plan 10–12/day, be ready for 18+. Lost sales understate true demand.

Costs: holding .067/unit/day; ordering .50; stockout 1.00/lost unit. Stockouts dominate; over-order.

Lead time: Orders take ~2 days. Receipts may arrive after daily sales, so same-day/next-day arrivals do not prevent stockout. “Arriving next 2 days” is not protection when on hand is low.

Policy:
- Target inventory position (on hand + on order) ~35–45. Covers 2 days at 12–18/day plus safety.
- Reorder when position falls below ~30. If stock 0–5, order 30–40 immediately, even if arrivals are scheduled.
- Do not order 0 when stock is 0. Day 22 lost 1 with arrivals [12,20]; Day 29 stock 2 arrivals [1,5] lost 22; Day 30 stock 0 arrivals [5,9] lost 14.
- 20-unit orders are now too small when stock is low: Day 26 stock 5, arrivals [6,0], demand 15, order 20 still lost 2. Day 23 order 20 was only just enough.
- If stock hits 0 before receipts, prioritize immediate large order. Do not wait for incoming.

Ops notes (racking, temp receiving, carrier pickup, cycle count) are irrelevant; counts matched system.

Current: stock often 0 before receipts. Maintain high buffer. If stock 0 and arrivals [5,9], order 35+ now.

WORKING NOTES — Inventory ordering

Demand has cooled. Recent 14-day sales: 11,0,18,3,5,3,1,3,2,5,1,5,6,2; avg ~4.6, but spikes 11–18 still possible. Older avg ~8.5. Lost sales understate true demand.

Costs: holding .067/unit/day; ordering .50; stockout 1.00/lost unit. Holding now dominates when overstocked; stockouts still costly.

Lead time ~2 days. Receipts may arrive after daily sales, so “arriving next 2 days” does not protect if on hand is low.

Policy:
- Target inventory position (on hand + on order) ~25–30, not 35–45. Covers ~2 days at recent demand plus spike safety.
- Reorder when position falls below ~20. Order enough to reach ~30.
- If stock 0–5, order 25–30 immediately. If arrivals already cover near-term need and demand is low, a smaller order may suffice. Do not wait for incoming if truly empty.
- Do not order when position is above ~30; let stock draw down.
- Avoid repeat 35+ orders unless demand spikes or stock is 0 with no near receipts. Day 31 order of 35 prevented stockout, but contributed to later stock of 49, 47, 42 and high holding costs.
- Days 32–40: no orders was correct while stock stayed above 28; all costs were holding, no stockouts.

Ops notes (racking, temp receiving, carrier pickup, cycle count) are irrelevant; counts matched system.

Current: Day 40 stock 28, no arrivals. Order 0. Reassess near position 20. If stock drops below 20, order ~10–15 to restore ~30. If stock 0–5, order ~25–30.
